rationale_summary: Late-cycle mix: sticky 3.4% CPI with 4.7% PPI, softening labor (-23k payrolls, downward revisions) and 1.5% Q2 GDP, with the FOMC on hold at 3.50-3.75% and three hawkish dissents. Heavy September event calendar (Aug 26 NVDA, Sep 4 payrolls, Sep 11 CPI, Sep 16 FOMC) creates two-sided risk. Few candidates show clean overreaction with independent support, so SPY-heavy positioning is appropriate.
portfolio_rationale: Only three candidates combine a genuine recent relative pullback with independent support: LARGE_VALUE and SMALL_VALUE show positive prior relative trends, low volatility and shallow drawdowns with the highest equity quality scores, and UTILITIES shows the deepest recent relative pullback with low beta ahead of a dense macro calendar. High-volatility momentum names (SMH, OIL, XME, SLV) and duration/credit lack in-window support given 3.4% CPI, 4.7% PPI and hawkish FOMC dissents. Edges are modest, so SPY remains the appropriate default for unfilled exposure.
key_risks: NVIDIA results on Aug 26 could drive a large index-level move that overwhelms modest factor tilts; September 16 FOMC and Sep 11 CPI could reprice rates sharply, hurting utilities and value simultaneously; Continued mega-cap leadership would keep cap-weighted SPY ahead of value and equal-weight tilts; Labor-market deterioration (payrolls -23k, benchmark revision Aug 28) could hit small-cap value hardest; Low VIX at 15.84 implies limited cushion for a volatility spike
